introduction: AHCCCS is Arizona’s Medicaid program. Health-e-Arizona Plus handles many applications, while older, disabled and long-term-care applicants have additional category-specific routes.

who: AHCCCS evaluates the applicable coverage category and financial and non-financial conditions. Family, pregnancy, adult, disability and long-term-care pathways differ.
Long-term care through ALTCS requires both financial and medical eligibility. Do not assume a general medical application requests all ALTCS services.
sections.get: Approved applicants receive health coverage for their category. Available plans depend on county and program, and provider networks differ. Check whether your doctor and pharmacy participate before selecting a plan.
sections.docs: Gather household, income and existing-insurance information. Use the appropriate application’s verification instructions. Applicants seeking disability, Medicare cost help or long-term care should ask about the additional records needed for that route.
sections.apply:
1. Use AHCCCS’s How to Apply page.
  2. For many applicants, apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus or the linked DES Application for Benefits.
  3. The page identifies DE-103 for specified older, blind/disabled and Medicare-cost-sharing applicants. ALTCS has a separate registration and interview process.
  4. Save confirmation, respond to requests and use a community assistor if you need help completing the application.
sections.after: Read the decision for category, effective date and enrollment details. When choosing a plan, compare its doctors and pharmacies in your county. Keep contact information current and follow renewal requests and reporting duties.

faqs: Can I choose my health plan?
Yes. Choose among plans available for your county and program. If you do not choose, a plan can be assigned.
Is ALTCS the same application route?
ALTCS uses a distinct registration and financial/medical review process explained on the AHCCCS application page.
AHCCCS links to community assistors who help with Health-e-Arizona Plus applications.
No. Plans cover the same basic services but have different provider networks. Confirm your provider before choosing.
